what_it_does: Large data centers use many servers, and a common cause of crashes is the failure of memory chips (called DRAM — the fast short-term storage inside a server). Predicting which memory chip will fail next lets operators swap it out before a crash happens. The wrinkle is that modern data centers mix two different families of processors — x86 (Intel/AMD) and ARM — and memory fails differently on each family. MemSeer analyzes these distinct failure patterns and builds a prediction model that works across both chip families, making predictions at several different time granularities (near-term versus longer-term) at once. The abstract claims it improves a standard accuracy measure (F1-score) by about 17% and catches 27% more failures that would otherwise be missed.
